summary.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 76.2% YoY to INR71.5 crores and PAT rose 124.1% to INR5.4 crores, with FY27 guided at INR180-200 crores.
summary.overview: Gabion posted its strongest first half since listing on BSE SME in January 2026, with consolidated revenue of INR71.53 crores (up 76.2%), EBITDA of INR10.27 crores (margin 14.4% vs 14.2%) and PAT of INR5.42 crores (margin 7.6% vs 6%). Operating cash flow was an outflow of INR5.69 crores as inventory and receivables rose, and net debt-to-equity reached 0.86. Management reiterated FY27 turnover guidance of INR180-200 crores, guided FY28 to INR300-350 crores, and said the Assam unit and Paonta Sahib expansion take group capacity to 18,000 MTPA.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR2.52 crores in H1 FY26

segments.name: Solutions (design-to-install projects)
segments.commentary: About 50% of H1 revenue; management says solutions PAT margin is roughly 5 percentage points higher than the supply business. Solutions is 79% private/EPC clients and 21% direct government in the order book.

segments.name: Supply (manufactured products)
segments.commentary: About 50% of H1 revenue. Tonnage in H1 was about 80% above the prior-year period, per management. Supply orders arrive monthly, with management expecting INR30-40 crores added to order book over the year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 turnover guidance INR180-200 crores (Q&A answers quoted INR185 crores as the low end, then INR180-200 crores); H2 revenue expected at about INR120 crores vs INR70 crores in H1.
FY28 turnover guidance INR300-350 crores; management says it expects to cross INR300 crores; about 50% growth or 50-100% range, with 60% cited as a point guidance.
Margins: FY27 margins expected to hold or rise slightly from H1 levels; FY28 PAT margin to improve by 1-2 percentage points.
PVC granule backward integration expected by end-FY27, conservatively Q1 FY28; management says it adds about 1% to PAT margin. GI wire backward integration under discussion, adding about 1.1% more.
Working capital expected to improve by about 10% by year-end; debt may rise INR10-15 crores by March 2027, with debt-to-equity to stay below 1.0.
Management expects 2 consecutive years of about 50% YoY growth and margin expansion of 1-2 percentage points per year.
capex_capacity: Assam unit near Guwahati (about 5,000 MTPA, with on-site PVC coating) is operational; ramp-up expected to full utilisation by December 2026.

Paonta Sahib: existing 9,200 MTPA certified plant plus new lines; machinery in transit, arriving December 2026; full 18,000 MTPA group capacity (with Assam and Nepal) conservatively from late January 2027. FY26 production was 9,108 tons.
Manufacturing capacity at full run-rate cited as capable of about INR150 crores revenue; solutions side another INR150 crores or more.

Net cash used in investing activities in H1 was INR4.86 crores, mainly for Assam unit and Paonta Sahib expansion. Management says all planned capex is now complete, apart from the machinery arriving in December.
Plans to bring PVC compound in-house (PVC granule backward integration) by end-FY27, conservatively Q1 FY28.
demand_pricing: Order book above INR120 crores as of the call date; 35 live work contracts total INR179.9 crores, of which INR69.4 crores billed and INR110.5 crores yet to be billed.
14 new work orders worth INR53.4 crores won between April and September 2026.

Order book: over half in rockfall and slope protection, then embankments and retaining walls, plus new ash pond work; spread across 11 states, led by Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Uttarakhand, Bihar, Himachal Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, with no state above one-fifth.

Bid pipeline: about INR200 crores of bids submitted, including government tenders; management expects about INR150 crores of new orders in FY27 (INR40-50 crores government, INR100 crores private), mostly executed in FY28.

Competition: small firms undercut on supply pricing, where Gabion competes on quality; larger firms compete on design and execution, where Gabion competes on technical capability and its ability to self-execute.
Standalone design orders received from Hindalco, NCC and D.H. Desai; management says designs will now be paid for upfront.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp H1 EBITDA margin expansion to about 22% and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Deepak Rajhans attributed it to lower employee cost, which he said fell from 14% to 10% of revenue, plus plant utilisation and inventory cost optimisation. He said margins will be stable in coming years. Note the 22% figure in the question does not match the 14.4% EBITDA margin reported.

qa_highlights.question: What was H1 volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Madhusudan Sarda said tonnage was about 80% above the same period last year, with about 50% of revenue from solutions and 50% from supply.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 and FY28 guidance, and why did it appear to rise?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 guidance is INR180-200 crores (INR185 crores low end). FY28 guidance is INR300-350 crores; management called it a wide range and said it expects FY28 to cross INR300 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Rishab Malik said finance cost fell YoY, from INR2.52 crores to INR2.09 crores, and the company is working to reduce it further. The analyst's premise of a sharp increase was not supported by the figures given.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin uplift do backward integration steps add?
qa_highlights.answer: PVC granule integration adds about 1 percentage point to PAT margin; GI wire integration adds about 1.1 percentage points more. Management described this path as taking PAT margin toward about 7%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the new mining and industrial (ash pond) vertical potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees INR200-300 crores over the next two to three years in this vertical, with live projects for Vedanta and JSW.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for working capital and debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is expected to improve by about 10% by year-end, with tighter collections and a larger recovery team. Debt may rise INR10-15 crores by March 2027, but debt-to-equity will stay below 1.0.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export and certification status?
qa_highlights.answer: The first rockfall product is expected to get European (CE/EN) certification in FY27, with all products by mid-FY28. Nettings are in talks with customers in Africa and the Middle East; European markets are targeted in FY28.

risks_watch: Working capital strain: H1 operating cash flow was an outflow of INR5.69 crores; receivables rose to INR43.91 crores and inventories to INR46.76 crores; net debt-to-equity is 0.86.
Execution: about 110.5 crores of the order book still to bill must be executed through peak season; the new Paonta Sahib machinery arrives in December and commissioning slips are possible.
Guidance step-up: FY28 guidance of INR300-350 crores is roughly 50-75% above the FY27 range; management guided a 60% growth figure in the call.
Government share: direct government work is 21% of the order book; the bid desk and larger government tenders are not yet proven.
Pricing pressure from small competitors in supply, and dependence on large EPC and private clients (79% of book).
Concentration of revenue-linked outcomes on certifications (European certification) and export orders, which are not yet secured.
Dependence on the Assam unit ramp-up by December 2026 and Paonta Sahib lines for capacity expansion.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth, capacity and outlook, with broad guidance ranges and some loose figures. Answers were less precise on volumes, margin and debt, and the call included several internal inconsistencies (e.g., FY27 guidance quoted as INR185-200 and INR180-200 crores; a 22% EBITDA margin question against 14.4% reported).
key_quotes: For us, listing is a commitment to earn that trust every half year through performance and transparency, and calls like this are part of keeping our commitment.
In our business, every completion certificate becomes the credential for the next larger tender.
Our trust is on getting the European certification for our rockfall protection products in this half of the year H2.

adds.what: Assam unit near Guwahati (about 5,000 MTPA, with on-site PVC coating)
Paonta Sahib new lines, taking group capacity to 18,000 MTPA (incl. Assam and Nepal); machinery arriving December 2026

growth.why: FY27 turnover guided at INR180-200 crores (about 190% growth on FY26 implied by H1 at INR71.5 cr plus H2 ~INR120 cr), backed by Assam unit ramp, Paonta Sahib machinery arriving December 2026, and an order book above INR120 crores; FY28 guided INR300-350 crores.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 EBITDA margin 14.4% vs 14.2%, management says FY27 margins hold or rise slightly, and PVC granule integration adds about 1pp to PAT margin by end-FY27 or Q1 FY28, with FY28 PAT margin up 1-2pp.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Paonta Sahib machinery arrives December 2026 and full 18,000 MTPA group capacity (incl. Assam ~5,000 MTPA, Nepal) conservatively from late January 2027, with Assam ramp to full utilisation by December 2026; FY26 Paonta Sahib production was 9,108 tons against a 9,200 MTPA certified plant.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 tonnage was about 80% above prior year and H2 revenue is guided at about INR120 crores vs INR70 crores in H1, with an order book above INR120 crores and FY28 guided at INR300-350 crores (about 50-60% growth).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says all planned capex is now complete apart from the December machinery, so no new capex is firmly planned, but GI wire backward integration is under discussion (adds about 1.1pp PAT margin) and utilisation is not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY28 guided INR300-350 crores and management expects to cross INR300 crores, but FY27 INR180-200 crores is only held and H2 must deliver about INR120 crores (1.7x H1) through peak season.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 operating cash flow was an outflow of INR5.69 crores, inventories rose to INR46.76 crores from INR35.50 crores, INR110.5 crores of the order book is still to bill, and Paonta Sahib machinery commissioning could slip past December 2026.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: First rockfall product expected to get European CE/EN certification in FY27 with all products by mid-FY28, and export nettings in talks in Africa and the Middle East, but none is yet secured.

rows.label: Order book conversion to FY27-28 revenue
rows.why: Order book above INR120 crores with 35 live contracts worth INR179.9 crores (INR110.5 crores unbilled) and about INR150 crores of new orders expected in FY27, mostly executed in FY28.

rows.label: Mining and ash pond vertical (Vedanta, JSW)
rows.why: Management sees INR200-300 crores potential over two to three years with live Vedanta and JSW projects, though the figure is management's own estimate.

rows.label: Working capital improvement by about 10%
rows.why: Management expects a 10% improvement by year-end after receivables of INR43.91 crores and inventories of INR46.76 crores rose in H1, with debt up INR10-15 crores and debt-to-equity kept below 1.0.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27-28 growth, capacity and margin path, but answers on volumes, margin drivers and debt were loose and contained inconsistencies (INR185 vs INR180 crores low end, a 22% margin question against 14.4% reported), which analysts pushed on.
